newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon hails first international credit ratings.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon hails first international credit ratings.

text.p: International agencies awarded Lebanon on Wednesday credit ratings for the first time on its long-term foreign currency debt obligations. They ranged from BB to BBB-.
The government said the ratings from Standard and Poor's, Moody's, IBCA and Nippon put Lebanon ahead of countries like Brazil and Turkey, and on a par with countries like Argentina and Jordan.
IBCA and S&P also assigned Lebanon local currency ratings of BBB- and BB respectively.
"These ratings place Lebanon ahead of Peru, Brazil, Bulgaria, Pakistan and Turkey and on a par with countries such as Argentina and Peru," a statement issued simultaneously in Beirut and London said.
It was issued in London by Merrill Lynch International which acted as adviser to the Lebanese government in obtaining the ratings.
The statement quoted a government spokesman as saying the ratings were important to Lebanon's reconstruction effort and would help it raise increased finance for reconstruction and investment.

"We feel that this is an important part of the continuing rehabilitation of the country both domestically and internationally and of the effort to increase the potential resources which could be mobilised for reconstruction and investment," the government spokesman said.

Merrill Lynch said the government's decision to obtain and publish the ratings "reflects its commitment to integrate itself into the world economy and in doing so subject itself to the scrutiny of international investors."
